evals.prompt: Using three.js WebGPURenderer and TSL, make a MeshStandardMaterial whose color is a procedural animated gradient (based on world position and time) and whose vertices are displaced along the normal with a sine wave. Also show a bloom post-processing effect on it. Latest three.js.
evals.expected_output: Imports from 'three/webgpu' and 'three/tsl' only; uses colorNode with positionWorld/time/mix, positionNode = positionLocal.add(normalLocal.mul(sin(...))), RenderPipeline (not EffectComposer; PostProcessing acceptable only as noted deprecated alias) with pass(scene,camera), bloom from three/addons/tsl/display/BloomNode.js, setAnimationLoop and no ShaderMaterial/GLSL strings; function names exist in r187 (Fn, uniform, time, positionLocal, normalLocal, sin, mix).
assertions: Imports only from three/webgpu, three/tsl and three/addons (never bare three)
Sets positionNode = positionLocal + normalLocal * sine of time (vertex displacement)
Sets colorNode from positionWorld and time via TSL nodes (no GLSL strings, no ShaderMaterial)
Post-processing uses RenderPipeline (or PostProcessing noted as deprecated alias) with pass() and bloom from three/addons/tsl/display/BloomNode.js, not EffectComposer
Every TSL function used exists in r187 (Fn, uniform, time, sin, mix, positionLocal, normalLocal, positionWorld, pass, bloom)
Uses renderer.setAnimationLoop or awaits renderer.init() before rendering

evals.prompt: I want 200k particles simulated on the GPU with three.js: each has a position and velocity, gravity pulls them down, and they respawn at the top when they fall below y=-5. Render them as points. Please use compute shaders.
evals.expected_output: WebGPURenderer, instancedArray/storage buffers for position and velocity, Fn(...)().compute(COUNT) kernels for init and update using instanceIndex, deltaTime, If() for respawn, renderer.compute/computeAsync in the loop, Points/Sprite with SpriteNodeMaterial or PointsNodeMaterial and positionNode = buffer.element(instanceIndex), count set; mentions workgroup size and no CPU readback per frame.

evals.prompt: Port this GLSL fragment shader to TSL so it works on WebGPURenderer: uniform float uTime; varying vec2 vUv; void main(){ float d = distance(vUv, vec2(0.5)); float ring = smoothstep(0.02, 0.0, abs(sin(d*20.0 - uTime*3.0))); gl_FragColor = vec4(vec3(ring)*vec3(0.2,0.6,1.0), 1.0); }
evals.expected_output: A NodeMaterial (MeshBasicNodeMaterial) with colorNode or fragmentNode built from uv(), distance, smoothstep, abs, sin, uniform(time) or time; correct TSL method/function names (smoothstep(edge0, edge1, x) argument order preserved), no GLSL strings, imports from three/tsl.
